response_text: The PendSV_Handler function executes a context switch when triggered by the pendable interrupt. The first step it executes is located the stack location of the current running thread, through reading the PSP of the current running thread. It then stores the registers R4-R11 of the current thread, which contain the context for the thread are pushed onto the stack to be stored. Next it calls the scheduling function osSched(). This function determines the next thread that should be run. Then it locates the new thread’s stack and sets the PSP to match the stack pointer of the next new thread which will be run. Next using the new updated value of PSP, the context for the new thread is popped into registers R4-R11 on the stack. This finishes the context switch that then allows the next thread to run.\n
